orphan-page.context: A small sitemap tree of linked page boxes with one extra page box standing alone to the side. Used for SEO audits that find pages with no internal links, and for site structure and crawl reports.

vote-arrows.context: An up chevron over the number one with a down chevron below it in a narrow column. Used for upvote and downvote controls on forums, comment threads, link aggregators and Q and A sites.

subscribe-button.context: A rounded button with a small bell on the left and a short text line on the right. Stands for subscribe, follow and notify me buttons on video channels, blogs and newsletters.

ban-hammer.context: A large hammer coming down on a round user avatar. Used for banning users, moderation tools, blocking accounts and community rule enforcement.

flame-war.context: Two speech bubbles facing each other with a flame rising between them. Shows heated arguments, trolling and toxic comment threads in forums and social media.

lurker.context: A pair of eyes peeking over the top edge of a browser window. Marks silent members who read but never post, passive visitors and forum watchers.

user-generated-content.context: A content block at the top with three small people below, each sending an arrow up into it. Used for ugc, community posts, reviews and crowd contributed content.

social-proof-notification.context: A small toast card with a round avatar and two text lines placed over lines of page text. Used for recent purchase and signup popups that show other people's activity on a site.

exit-intent-popup.context: A cursor leaving the top of a browser window while a modal box pops up in the middle of the page. Used for exit intent offers, last chance discounts and cart saving overlays.

newsletter-popup.context: A modal box over a page holding an envelope, an input line and a button. Used for email capture popups, newsletter signup overlays and mailing list prompts.

form-abandonment.context: A half filled form with a small walking figure moving away from it. Used for analytics about people who start but never finish a form, signup or checkout.

cart-drawer.context: A browser window with a panel sliding in from the right that shows a small shopping cart and an item line. Used for slide out mini carts and side basket panels in online shops.

promo-code-field.context: An input field with a small coupon ticket on the left and a tick on the right. Used for entering and applying discount, voucher and promo codes at checkout.

abandoned-cart.context: A shopping cart standing alone with a small cobweb in the corner above it. Used for abandoned basket reports, cart recovery emails and checkout drop off analytics.

custom-domain.context: An address bar joined by a short line to a globe below it. Used for connecting your own domain name to a site, store or app, and for branded web addresses.

dns-propagation.context: A globe with ripple arcs spreading out from one point on its surface. Used for DNS update status, nameserver changes and waiting for a domain change to reach the world.

dns-record.context: A small globe above a table with three rows and a label column next to a value column. Used for DNS zone settings such as A, CNAME and MX records.

subdomain.context: A large globe with a branch line leading down to two smaller globes. Used for subdomains such as blog.example.com and for splitting a site into parts.

top-level-domain.context: A tag shape holding a bold dot followed by three short strokes for letters. Used for domain endings such as .com, .org and .net, and for TLD registries and searches.

whois-record.context: A globe peeking above an ID card with a head silhouette and text lines. Used for domain ownership lookups and registration details.

domain-for-sale.context: A globe with a price tag hanging beside it. Used for domain marketplaces, parked names offered for purchase and domain auctions.

parked-domain.context: A globe with a square parking sign showing the letter P standing next to it. Used for domains that are registered but not yet in use.

domain-transfer.context: Two globes with an arrow carrying a small tag from the upper left over to the right. Used for moving a domain from one registrar to another.

localhost.context: A laptop with a circular arrow looping inside its screen. Stands for localhost, the local machine and a development server that talks to itself.

shared-hosting.context: One server box with three small houses sitting on top of it. Shows web hosting where several websites share the same server.

virtual-private-server.context: A server box split into three compartments by dashed walls with the middle one filled in. Used for VPS plans and isolated virtual machines on shared hardware.

hosting-control-panel.context: A browser window filled with a grid of six small tiles. Used for hosting dashboards such as cPanel and for site and server management screens.

ftp-transfer.context: A folder and a server side by side with two opposite arrows between them. Used for FTP and SFTP file uploads and downloads to a remote host.

http-header.context: A message page with a header band holding three pairs of short key and value lines. Used for HTTP request and response headers and metadata.

url-encoding.context: An address bar with percent signs placed between short text segments. Used for percent encoding, escaped characters and query string handling in links.

preview-deployment.context: A browser window with an eye in the page and a small branch mark beside it. Used for staging builds and pull request previews before a site goes live.

webmail.context: A browser window with an envelope in the middle of the page. Stands for email read in a web browser rather than a desktop app.

mail-server.context: Two stacked server units with an envelope in front of the lower corner. Used for SMTP and IMAP servers and hosted email infrastructure.

email-template.context: An envelope next to a page showing a header block, an image block and two text lines. Used for newsletter layouts and email design templates.

drip-campaign.context: A faucet dripping a line of small envelopes downward. Stands for automated email sequences that send messages one at a time over days or weeks.

email-autoresponder.context: An envelope with a small robot head above its flap. Used for automatic replies, out of office messages and instant confirmation emails.

unsubscribe-link.context: An envelope with an exit door bracket and an outward arrow at its lower right. Used for opt out links and leave this mailing list controls.

double-opt-in.context: An envelope with two check marks stacked beside it. Used for confirming a newsletter signup by clicking a link in a confirmation email.

lead-magnet.context: A horseshoe magnet pulling a small open book up toward its poles. Stands for free guides and ebooks offered in exchange for an email address.

email-subscriber.context: A person bust holding an envelope in front of the chest. Used for newsletter readers, mailing list members and email contacts.

spam-filter.context: A funnel with several small envelopes entering the top and a mesh line inside it. Used for junk mail filtering and inbox protection settings.

email-deliverability.context: An envelope flying along a curved path into an inbox tray. Used for inbox placement, delivery rates and sender reputation reports.

bounced-email.context: An envelope hitting a wall on the right and bouncing back along a curved arrow. Used for undeliverable messages, failed sends and bounce reports.

transactional-email.context: An envelope with a receipt slip with a torn top edge sticking out of it. Used for order confirmations, receipts, password resets and other automatic one to one emails.

welcome-email.context: An open envelope with a waving hand rising out of it. Used for the first email sent to a new subscriber or customer.

email-warmup.context: An envelope beside a thermometer with a small flame in its bulb. Used for gradually building a sending reputation for a new address or IP.

spam-score.context: A semicircle gauge with a needle and a small envelope under its pivot. Used for spam rating checks that test how likely an email is to land in junk.

email-open-rate.context: An open envelope with a percent sign inside its raised flap. Used for campaign metrics showing what share of recipients opened an email.

tag-manager.context: An open box with three small tags standing out over its rim. Used for tag management tools that hold tracking scripts and marketing pixels in one place.

event-tracking.context: An arrow cursor clicking with ripple arcs beside a column of three dots. Used for click and interaction tracking and custom analytics events.

data-layer.context: Three stacked flat layers with small code chevrons on the top layer. Used for the data layer that passes page and user data to tag managers.

tracking-snippet.context: Code angle brackets with a small eye between them. Used for tracking code, analytics scripts and tracking pixels embedded in a page.

user-session.context: A browser window with a small person avatar and a stopwatch side by side. Used for visit length, session duration and session replay in web analytics.

unique-visitors.context: A row of three people where the middle one has a fingerprint on the chest. Used for unique visitor and distinct user counts in analytics.

exit-page.context: A browser page with an arrow leaving through its right edge. Used for the last page visitors see before leaving a site.

returning-visitor.context: A person with a looping arrow curling back up toward a small browser window. Used for repeat visitors and return visits in analytics.

cross-device-tracking.context: A phone, a laptop and a tablet joined by dotted lines to one person above. Used for recognising the same user across several devices.

search-intent.context: A magnifying glass with a small thought bubble above it. Used for the goal behind a search query, such as informational or transactional intent.

knowledge-panel.context: Search result lines on the left and a tall boxed card with an image block on the right. Used for the information box that appears beside search results about a person, place or brand.

sitelinks.context: One bold result line with a two by two grid of short link lines indented under it. Used for the extra links shown under a main search result.

search-snippet.context: A single search result with a bold title line, a short address line and two text lines. Used for how a page appears in search results.

rich-snippet.context: A search result with a small thumbnail, a title line and a row of five stars under it. Used for enhanced results with ratings and structured data.

meta-tag.context: A tag shape with angle brackets drawn on its face. Used for HTML meta tags, page metadata and SEO descriptions.

title-tag.context: A browser tab shape with a bold capital T inside it. Used for the HTML page title that shows in tabs and search results.

keyword-research.context: A magnifying glass hovering over a key. Used for finding search terms and keyword ideas for content and SEO planning.

keyword-stuffing.context: A page bulging at the sides with words and tags spilling out of the top. Used for the spam tactic of cramming too many keywords into content.

keyword-difficulty.context: A key lying under a semicircle gauge with the needle pointing high. Used for scores showing how hard it is to rank for a search term.

search-volume.context: A magnifying glass with three rising bars inside its lens. Used for how many times a term is searched each month.

search-ranking.context: A three step podium with a magnifying glass on the top step. Used for search result position and rank tracking.

domain-authority.context: A globe with a semicircle gauge above it and the needle near full. Used for site strength scores that estimate how well a domain can rank.

organic-traffic.context: A leaf with an upward trending arrow running along its midrib. Used for free visitors from search engines and natural growth in traffic.

geotargeting.context: A target ring with crosshair ticks and a map pin in the centre. Used for targeting content and ads by location or radius.

seo-audit.context: A clipboard with rising bars and a magnifying glass over its corner. Used for site checks that list SEO problems and improvements.

search-index.context: A card catalog drawer with index cards and a magnifying glass resting on top. Used for pages stored in a search engine index and crawl status.

search-engine-optimization.context: A magnifying glass with an upward arrow rising through its lens. Stands for SEO and improving how high a site ranks in search.

pillar-page.context: A large central page joined by short lines to four smaller pages around it. Used for pillar content and topic clusters that link to supporting articles.

evergreen-content.context: A page with a small evergreen pine tree in its lower half. Used for timeless articles that stay relevant and keep drawing traffic over years.

win-back-email.context: An envelope above a curved arrow that swings back like a boomerang. Used for re-engagement emails sent to lapsed subscribers and inactive customers.

html-email.context: An envelope with angle bracket code tags and a slash printed on its front. Used for coded and responsive email design and email development.
